steps.exitTrigger: Assembly SOP released and operators trained
steps.entryQuestion: Is the assembly process documented to the level a line operator needs?
steps.exitQuestion: Can an operator with no product knowledge follow it correctly?
steps.whatToDo: Add the assembly SOP section: every operation with its acceptance criteria, tooling and operator instruction.
steps.guidelines: Write the SOP at operator level: step by step, with photographs, torque values, orientation checks and inspection points. Include what to do when something does not fit rather than leaving it to judgement, because judgement at the station is where undocumented variation enters. Confirm operators are trained against it and that the training is recorded.

steps.entryTrigger: Firmware released and flashing procedure validated at pilot
steps.exitTrigger: Code flashing SOP released and station set up
steps.entryQuestion: Is the flashing procedure documented and proven at volume?
steps.exitQuestion: Are firmware versions, hashes and file locations unambiguous in the document?
steps.whatToDo: Update the provisioning plan into a line SOP: station setup, sequence, timing, and the recovery path for a unit that fails mid-cycle.
steps.guidelines: Document the flashing procedure with exact firmware versions, hashes and file locations, the connection method, the sequence and the verification step. State the result recording requirement per serial number. Ambiguity about which file to flash is how a batch reaches the field with the wrong build, and traceability is the only thing that makes that recoverable.

steps.entryTrigger: Test procedures validated and fixtures available
steps.exitTrigger: Testing SOP released and test stations qualified
steps.entryQuestion: Is every production test documented with unambiguous pass and fail criteria?
steps.exitQuestion: Are pass and fail criteria numeric, and is the fixture calibrated?
steps.whatToDo: Add the testing SOP: every production test with unambiguous pass and fail criteria and the action on a fail.
steps.guidelines: Document each production test with setup, procedure, numeric pass and fail limits, and the action on failure. Include the production safety and functional tests where they apply: hipot at 3000 V AC for one second as a routine test, insulation resistance of 10 MΩ at 500 V DC, earth continuity at 25 A, earth bond below 0.1 Ω, touch current below 0.25 mA. The fixture must not bypass the insulation under test, and calibration must be current and recorded.

steps.step: Production DFT — test coverage versus fixture verification
steps.entryTrigger: Fixtures built and test procedures validated on real units
steps.exitTrigger: Measured coverage on the real fixture compared against the design-time coverage figure, with every shortfall dispositioned
steps.entryQuestion: Does the fixture actually reach what the design promised it would reach?
steps.exitQuestion: Where coverage fell short of the design figure, is there a documented alternative method or an accepted risk?
steps.whatToDo: Measure coverage again on the fixture that was actually built and compare it against the design-time figure. Every shortfall gets an alternative method or a written risk acceptance.
steps.guidelines: Take the coverage figure computed at layout and measure it again on the fixture that was built. They will not match — probes miss, pads oxidise, the support plate blocks something. Every net that the fixture does not reach in practice goes back onto the register with either an alternative method or a written risk acceptance. A coverage number claimed at design time and never verified is a number nobody should quote.

steps.entryTrigger: Labelling and marking artwork approved and compliance marks confirmed
steps.exitTrigger: Labelling SOP released with artwork and placement specified
steps.entryQuestion: Are all required regulatory and traceability markings defined and approved?
steps.exitQuestion: Are all compliance marks correct for the target markets and correctly placed?
steps.whatToDo: Add the labelling and marking SOP: every mark required by every target market, its position, and how it is verified.
steps.guidelines: Specify every marking with its artwork, placement, size and durability: compliance marks for the target markets, ratings, serial number, batch code, date code and any client branding. Verify compliance marks against the actual certificates — a mark applied without the corresponding certificate is a regulatory offence in most markets, not merely an error. Define the serial number scheme and how it is recorded for traceability.

steps.entryTrigger: Packaging specified and logistics route defined
steps.exitTrigger: Delivery SOP released with packaging and documentation specified
steps.entryQuestion: Is packaging validated to protect the product through the actual transit route?
steps.exitQuestion: Has the packaging been transit-tested for the real route and handling?
steps.whatToDo: Create the delivery schedule to client: quantities, dates, packing configuration and the documents accompanying each shipment.
steps.guidelines: Specify packaging, carton quantities, pallet configuration, labelling and the shipping documentation set. Validate the packaging against the real transit route rather than assuming — transit damage is expensive, disputes over liability are worse, and both are avoided by a drop and vibration test on the actual packed configuration. Define the delivery challan and its generation from the PO or PI.

steps.entryTrigger: Production units available and pre-compliance passed in-house
steps.exitTrigger: Compliance testing complete at an accredited laboratory
steps.entryQuestion: Has pre-compliance testing passed in-house before booking the lab?
steps.exitQuestion: Did the unit pass, and is the tested configuration the one that will ship?
steps.whatToDo: Record the production compliance testing against the shipping configuration.
steps.guidelines: Never book a formal lab slot without passing pre-compliance in-house first — a formal failure costs the slot, the retest fee and typically six weeks. Present a unit in the exact shipping configuration including enclosure, cables and packaging, since the tested configuration is the certified configuration and any later change requires reassessment. Attend the test where possible so a marginal result can be addressed on the spot.

steps.exitTrigger: Certificates issued and registered
steps.entryQuestion: Is the certification filing package complete for every target market?
steps.exitQuestion: Are the certificates issued in the correct legal entity name for the target markets?
steps.whatToDo: Add the production certificates to the register with their scope, expiry and the build revision covered.
steps.guidelines: File the complete package for each market — BIS or IS, FCC, CE declaration of conformity, UL as applicable — and check the applicant entity name is correct, since a certificate in the wrong name is not transferable and the correction takes months. Register the certificates against the project and confirm any post-approval change is assessed before release. File the marking artwork to match.

steps.exitTrigger: Project formally closed with learnings captured
steps.entryQuestion: Are all deliverables accepted, invoices raised and documentation handed over?
steps.exitQuestion: Has the code and documentation handover pack been transferred and acknowledged?
steps.whatToDo: Create the closure record: what was delivered, against which revisions, what remains open and who owns each open item.
steps.guidelines: Close properly: confirm all deliverables accepted, invoices raised and paid, and the code docket and documentation handover pack transferred with acknowledgement of receipt and version. That handover pack is the defined end point of engineering obligation — after it, documentation is the source of information and support scope is whatever the contract states. Update project status in the trackers, register proven components and blocks in the Component Database, and write the learnings document. A failure that does not change a document will happen again.

steps.step: DFM/DFT Gate G3 review and production release sign-off
steps.entryTrigger: DFMEA, PFMEA, DFMA and MFA complete and fixture coverage verified
steps.exitTrigger: G3 released — production safety, functional test, coating, marking and compliance checks all closed, with G0 to G2 also still released
steps.entryQuestion: Is the line, the fixture, the paperwork and the marking all ready, or only the design?
steps.exitQuestion: Does the Dashboard show G3 as RELEASE with every gate above it also released, and is the checklist signed by Production and QA?
steps.whatToDo: Confirm G3 shows RELEASE with every earlier gate still released, then sign with Production and QA present. A late component change can reopen G1 without anyone noticing.
steps.guidelines: G3 is the product gate, not the board gate. It covers the things a working prototype never proves — production safety testing, marking and labelling, coating, compliance paperwork, and the closure of the FMEA actions. Sign it with Production and QA present, and check that the earlier gates are still released; a late component change can reopen G1 without anyone noticing.

steps.step: Audit Checklist update — EMS Requirements tab
steps.exitTrigger: EMS Requirements tab completed and shared with the manufacturing partner
steps.entryQuestion: Does the EMS have every document it needs to build without asking?
steps.exitQuestion: Has the EMS confirmed receipt and acceptance of the requirements tab?
steps.whatToDo: Complete the EMS Requirements tab and get written confirmation of receipt and acceptance from the manufacturing partner.
steps.guidelines: Complete the EMS tab and get written confirmation of receipt and acceptance. The Customer Extract view exists for exactly this — share the shared-visibility rows without exposing internal columns. An EMS that starts building against an unacknowledged pack will build to its own assumptions.

steps.step: Audit Checklist final closure and revision freeze
steps.entryTrigger: Mass production released and first shipment dispatched
steps.exitTrigger: Audit Checklist closed, frozen as a PDF baseline and filed as the project exit record
steps.entryQuestion: Is every Required row closed or formally waived with a named accepter?
steps.exitQuestion: Is the frozen copy stored, and does it name the revision of every artefact it certifies?
steps.whatToDo: Freeze a PDF baseline alongside the live file, recording the revision of every artefact it certifies. This is the project's exit record.
steps.guidelines: Freeze a PDF baseline alongside the live file and record the revision of every artefact it certifies. This frozen copy is the project's exit record and the document you will reach for in a warranty dispute, a re-certification or a repeat order. A live sheet that keeps moving cannot serve as evidence of what was true at release.

steps.step: DFM/DFT checklist closure and house standard update
steps.entryTrigger: G3 released and the first production run complete
steps.exitTrigger: Checklist frozen as the project's DFx record, and every finding the checklist did not already ask for added to the house standard
steps.entryQuestion: What did this project teach us that the checklist did not already ask?
steps.exitQuestion: Has the house standard been updated, versioned and issued so the next project starts from it?
steps.template: DFM/DFT Lessons Learned and House Standard Update
steps.whatToDo: Create the lessons sheet and turn every problem found outside the checklist into a proposed new check with a gate, a severity and a parameter. Then version the house standard.
steps.guidelines: Freeze a copy of the completed checklist as the project record, then do the part everybody skips: take the problems that were found outside the checklist and turn each one into a new check with a gate, a severity and, where a number is involved, a parameter. A checklist that never grows is a checklist that keeps missing the same things. Version the house standard and tell the next project it changed.
